newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks close slightly lower, banks up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close slightly lower, banks up.

text.p: - Hong Kong stocks inched to a slightly lower close on Friday, ending a record-breaking week on a firm note with brokers convinced the market's rally would push it throught the 17,000 barrier early next week.

"The market performed quite well despite the sharp fall in Wall Street overnight," said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Securities. "We were down more than 180 points in the morning session, but bargain hunting brought us right back up."
The Hang Seng Index closed 25.73 points, or 0.15 percent, lower at 16,647.54, clawing back from a morning dive to 16,482.02.
Turnover dipped to a still-weighty HK$23.37 billion.
The index's pullback was viewed as a needed correction, after nearly two weeks of record-breaking market activity, brokers said.
On Thursday, the markets set a record close of 16,673.27 after hitting an all-time high of 16,820.31 on record single-day turnover of HK$34.2 billion.
The Dow Industrials shed 71.31 points to close at 8,188.00 on concerns over higher U.S. interest rates on Thursday.
"There was no significant selling today, said To. "We could see another strong rise to 17,000 next week."
Technically, the market was still overbought.
"That doesn't mean the market couldn't rise another 100 or even 1,000 points," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities.
But divergences between some technical indicators and the index's uptrend, suggested the index could pull back a couple of hundred points to digest the previous upside move, Shum said.
Only the finance sector managed to buck the downtrend, while the commercial and industrial sector led the market down.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings closed HK$2.00 higher at HK$274.00 on renewed London buying interest, brokers said.
The Bank of East Asia added HK$0.30 to close at HK$31.20, while Hang Seng Bank slipped HK$0.50 to HK$103.00.
Among the conglomerates, Wharf shed HK$1.00 to close at HK$33.60. Hutchison Whampoa the focus on market attention throughout the week, eased HK$0.50 to HK$80.75.

CITIC Pacific hit a new high of HK$52.00, then fell back to close HK$1.35 higher at HK$51.25, chiefly on market talk that the company would sell all or part of its stake in Cathay to China National Aviation Corp (CNAC).
